newsitem.title: SPAIN: ATHLETICS-FIDATOV SEIZES SECOND CHALLENGE VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-FIDATOV SEIZES SECOND CHALLENGE VICTORY.

text.p: Romanian Elena Fidatov became the first runner to notch two wins in this season's International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) world cross challenge with a sprint finish to take the 5.45-km women's race on Sunday.
Fidatov crossed the line in 18 minutes three seconds with world champion Gete Wami, from Ethiopia, having to settle for second in 18:05. Spain's Julia Vacquero was third in 18:07.
Despite Fidatov's victories, in Amorebieta and in Belfast last week, Wami stays top of the cross challenge standings after four races.
The Ethiopian, who has run in all four races, has 85 points. Fidatov missed the opening race in Brussels last month and is second with 72 points.
The 10.85-km men's race was won by Kenya's David Chelule, the world junior champion, in 33 minutes 45 seconds.
Chelule pulled away from his three closest rivals about a kilometre from the finish. One second covered the next three places after a furious battle in the closing stages.
Kenya's James Moiben was second in 33:50 with Ethiopia's Hapte Jifar getting the verdict for third over Tanzania's Benedict Ako. Both runners were given the same time of 33:51.
France's Yann Millon moves to the top of the overall standings with 57 points, despite finishing 11th.
The world cross challenge is a 12-race series and has a $25,000 first prize for both the men's and women's winners. The next race is in Seville, Spain, next Sunday.
